rationale: Add a sequential-confirmation control to the fixed harness. The established failure used a later context confirmation to return an earlier remote request; the control queues the same two contexts but confirms the earlier admitted context first, then routes the produced reply through the same real follower handler and pendingReadIndex consumer. This distinguishes a context-association defect from a harness or consumer failure. A separate retained successor execution is requested; no control interpretation is asserted before its receipt.

scope.description: Sequential-confirmation control in the same three-peer in-process Raft group. Context A is queued before context B, but A is confirmed first; the resulting reply is routed through node 2's real follower handler and pendingReadIndex consumer.
assumptions: Real in-process Raft Peer handlers, a test-only in-memory ILogDB, and the same bootstrap membership {1,2,3} as the failing case.
Both requests are queued at the leader before confirmation. The heartbeat carrying node 2's context A is delivered to node 2 and its response returned to the leader before context B is confirmed.
The control uses the same pending-read consumer and applies the ReadyToRead index returned by node 2's follower handler.
Production code is unchanged; only message ordering and the test storage backend are controlled.
excluded: This control does not exercise disk persistence, restart, snapshots, real transport delay, or a later-confirmation race.
It is a comparison control for the main ordering case, not a separate defect claim.

experiment.prefix: The harness launches three real internal/raft Peer instances with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and a test-only in-memory ILogDB. Node 1 is ticked until its current-term no-op is committed. Node 2 and node 3 issue real ReadIndex requests with contexts A and B. The test delivers heartbeat A to node 2 and returns its real HeartbeatResp to leader 1 before context B is confirmed. Leader 1 produces a ReadIndex response for node 2; the test routes that response through node 2's real follower handler, feeds the resulting ReadyToRead to the pendingReadIndex consumer, applies its index, and checks the client request.
experiment.requirement: When the admitted context is the one confirmed first, the remote reply must carry that same SystemCtx and the applied ReadyToRead must complete the pending read through the same consumer path.
experiment.responsibility: The leader constructs the ReadIndex response in handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation; the requesting node's real follower handler and pendingReadIndex consume it. The control keeps the production handlers and changes only the order in which the two legal confirmations are delivered.

comparisons.description: The control reply must carry the context node 2 admitted.
The admitted read should complete when its own context is confirmed and its ready index is applied.

knowledge.assertion: The confirming context returns earlier queued requests while preserving each request's own SystemCtx.
Remote replies are tagged with the confirming heartbeat context instead of the queued request's context.
A response with a nonmatching SystemCtx leaves the original pending batch at index zero and cannot complete it.

experiment.revision_reason: Add a sequential-confirmation control to distinguish the later-first context mismatch from a harness or pending-read consumer failure.
